AT JABALPUR
BEFORE  HON'BLE SMT. JUSTICE ANURADHA SHUKLA  ON THE 17 th OF JANUARY, 2024  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 55345 of 2023

BETWEEN:-
 BRAJESH PATEL S/O SHRI KAMLESHWAR PATEL, AGED  ABOUT 26 YEARS, OCCUPATION: AGRICULTURIST R/O  VILLAGE DHANGADH P.S. DEVTALAB DISTRICT REWA  (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI R. N. CHATURVEDI - ADVOCATE)
 AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH POLICE  S TA T I O N CRIME BRANCH DISTRICT BHOPAL  (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI RAGUVAR PRAJAPATI - PANEL LAWYER)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the c  following:

ORDER This is third bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, for grant of bail relating to FIR/Crime No.25/2023 dated 15.03.2023 registered at Police Station- Crime Branch, District- Bhopal, for the offences punishable under Sections 419, 420 of Indian Penal Code and Section 66-C, 66-D of I.T. Act.
2.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody since 19.03.2023 and the trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
The applicant is the permanent resident of district and there is no possibility of his absconding or tampering with prosecution evidence.
He is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the conditions to be imposed by the Court.
Upon these grounds, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.

sentences.text: 3. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
5.
In this third application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. the applicant has requested for bail on the ground of his long custodial period.
According to him, against a maximum term of punishment of seven years, he is languishing in jail for last ten months.

The order sheets placed on record reveal that the evidence of both the sides was declared closed and at the stage of final arguments, an application moved by prosecution under Section 311 of Cr.P.C. was allowed, under which permission to examine only two additional witnesses was granted and it cannot be contended that the trial proceeded so far was at any rate slow or lax.

6. Considering the fact that earlier two bail applications of applicant were dismissed on merits vide detailed orders passed in M.Cr.C. Nos.22685/2023 and 31419/2023 and also the fact that applicant has not been able to show any unnecessary delay in the trial, this Court does not find it appropriate to release the applicant on bail.
7. Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands dismissed.

(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE pnm Brjesh Patel vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62928576/
